newsitem.title: USA: Lower Colo. River hydropower flows raised slightly.
newsitem.headline: Lower Colo. River hydropower flows raised slightly.

text.p: Flows through hydroelectric dams on the Lower Colorado River will be slightly increased through the end of March to make room for projected spring inflows, the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation said Friday.
The Bureau said an increase in projected April-July snowmelt runoff into Lake Powell, Utah, means higher than average releases from Hoover, Davis and Parker Dams at least thorugh March.
Weekday releases through Hoover Dam will increase to 19,400 cubic feet per second (cfs), from 19,000 cfs currently.
Releases through Davis Dam during weekdays will rise to 18,570 cfs from 17,300 cfs and Parker dam flows will be increased to 14,200 cfs from 13,200 cfs.
Flows through Hoover and Davis will be lower than those levels on weekends.
Releases through the Glen Canyon Dam are scheduled to remain unchanged at 24,000 cfs through mid-April.

The Colorado River Forecasting Service raised its projection of April-July runoff into Lake Powll to 171 percent of normal, or around 13.2 million acre feet (maf), compared with a mid-January forecast of 155 percent (12 maf).
